changelog: Add: During Open Position check-ins are now append-only (new trade_checkins/trade_checkin_actions tables), fixing the reported bug where reopening a trade showed the During section blank -- trade_journal's UNIQUE KEY (trade_id, phase) meant a second check-in silently overwrote the first, leaving only ever one row to reload. Each save now compares the submitted selections against the trade's own latest check-in and only inserts a new row when something actually differs -- saving other fields (notes, strategy, post-close) with During untouched creates no new row. A read-only, newest-first timeline of every check-in now renders below the During section in the edit form and in the read-only trade detail view. Existing during-phase trade_journal data is backfilled into trade_checkins, not discarded
Fix: the trade modal's save button always read 'Save Trade', even when editing an existing trade. Now reads 'Update Trade' when editing, 'Save Trade' when adding

Add: Pre-Entry Journal (setup grade, stop/target, pre-entry emotion, 'what would have to happen for me to be wrong') is now locked once a trade closes (result is Win/Loss/Break Even) -- it records what was planned before entry and must not be editable in hindsight. Enforced server-side in TradeController::saveJournal() (a locked pre_entry submission is silently ignored, not errored -- the rest of the save still goes through) and mirrored client-side for UX signal only, using readonly rather than disabled on stop_loss/take_profit specifically because a disabled input is dropped from FormData entirely and v3.16.1 B3 requires both fields on every save

Add: helpers.php::computeTradeRiskFields() now derives exit_quality='open' for any trade whose result isn't yet Win/Loss/Break Even, checked before the existing target_r-null branch -- previously an unresolved trade and a genuinely closed trade with no stop/target on file both landed on the same 'unknown' label. Backfilled for every currently-open trade; BitfundedImportController::confirm() needed no change since it already recomputes exit_quality right after setting a matched row's real result, so importing a close moves a trade from 'open' to a real computed value automatically
